# Appeal of Denial – Cervical Fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551

**Member:** Rowan Delgado
**Member ID:** W865123628
**Plan:** Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Dakota (Commercial/ACA)
**Denial date:** 2026-08-18
**Reference number:** POC-9391F374E1-41425
**Governing policy:** Cervical Fusions, S-9004-02 (https://www.bcbsnd.com/providers/policies-precertification/legacy-medical-policy/c/cervical-fusions), effective 2024-07-01

To Whom It May Concern:

I am writing to appeal the denial of my requested neck (cervical) fusion surgery (ACDF, CPT 22551), which was denied on 2026-08-18 as not medically necessary (reference number POC-9391F374E1-41425). My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to reconsider this decision in light of its own published criteria and the records already submitted.

## The Plan's Own Criteria and How My Records Meet Them

The plan's policy, Cervical Fusions, S-9004-02, states:

> "ACDF) is considered medically necessary for treatment of symptomatic degenerative disease when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

The policy then requires:

> "unremitting cervical radiculopathy and/or myelopathy (i.e., neck and arm pain) resulting in disability and/or neurological deficit that are refractory to at least six weeks of standard conservative, nonoperative management (e.g., reduced activities, exercise, analgesics, physical therapy), in the absence of progressive or severe myelopathy complex imaging studies (i.e., CT, MRI, X-ray) demonstrate at least ONE of the following at each impacted level being considered for the fusion:"

My records show this criterion is met. I have had 14 months of progressive neck pain with radicular pain, numbness, and weakness into my right thumb and index finger. I completed 18 visits of supervised physical therapy, including cervical traction and postural training, over 8 weeks (2026-05-18 to 2026-07-13) — well beyond the six weeks the policy requires. I also used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-08 gave only 3 weeks of partial relief. This is not progressive or severe myelopathy; it is radiculopathy that has not responded to sustained conservative care.

The policy also requires imaging showing at least one of the following at the affected level:

> " Herniated nucleus pulposus  Spondylosis (i.e., presence of osteophytes)  Visible loss of disc height compared to adjacent levels with resultant foraminal stenosis physical examination findings and imaging studies correlate with each level being considered for the fusion"

My MRI of the cervical spine, dated 2026-06-26, shows a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression — squarely within the imaging findings the policy lists. In addition, my physical exam showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit that corresponds to the imaged level, which is the correlation the policy requires between examination findings and imaging.

Based on the plan's own language, each element of the ACDF medical-necessity criteria appears to be documented in my chart: unremitting radiculopathy refractory to more than six weeks of conservative management, qualifying imaging findings at the affected level, and correlating physical exam findings. I am asking the plan to explain, specifically, which of these criteria it found unmet, since the denial notice does not identify a specific missing element.

## Request for the Criteria Applied

Because the denial states only that my case did not meet "the plan's criteria for medical necessity" without identifying which specific criterion was not satisfied, I am requesting that the plan provide, in writing, the complete criteria it applied to my case, along with an explanation of how those criteria were applied to my specific clinical records. I understand BCBSND publishes its medical policies on its Medical Policy Search page, searchable by CPT code, but I am asking that the specific criteria and reasoning used in my case be sent to me directly in writing as part of this appeal.

## What I Am Asking For

I respectfully ask that the plan reverse this denial and approve the requested ACDF (CPT 22551), based on the documentation already submitted by my surgeon and summarized above. If any additional records or clarification would help the plan complete its review, please let me know what is needed and I will work with my surgeon's office to provide it promptly.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-14. I am submitting it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; if that address is not available to me, I will call the number on the back of my insurance card to confirm where member appeals are filed.

Thank you for reconsidering my case.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Rowan Delgado
Member ID: W865123628
Date: [DATE]
Contact phone/email: [PHONE/EMAIL]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

evidence.submission_route: Use the appeal address printed on your denial letter, or call the number on the back of your insurance card and ask where member appeals are filed.
evidence.criteria_request: BCBSND writes and publishes its own criteria, free and login-free, but the search runs on JavaScript so a direct link often fails. Open the Medical Policy Search page and search by your CPT code.
